news_results.title: Posts on X

stories.snippet:
Only capitalism's mouthpiece, the New York Times, would come up with this. They are blaming public criticisms of the health insurance industry for the murder of the CEO:

www.nytimes.com/2024/12/05/nyregion/social-media-insurance-industry-brian-thompson.html

🚨UPDATE: Below are photos of a person of interest wanted for questioning regarding the Midtown Manhattan homicide on Dec. 4. This does not appear to be a random act of violence; all indications are that it was a premediated, targeted attack. 

The full investigative efforts of… pic.x.com/K3kzC4IbtS

That a brazen murder elicits more glee than outrage speaks to deep public resentment of the US health-insurance industry, which profits by erecting obstacles before people seeking payment for healthcare. The more people who give up, the bigger the profits. www.nytimes.com/2024/12/06/opinion/united-health-care-ceo-shooting.html?smid=nytcore-ios-share&referringSource=articleShare

I’ve heard from people who knew and loved and are grieving Brian Thompson. But it’s been impossible to miss the cheers over the UnitedHealthcare CEO’s murder.

I tried to take a look at this shocking moment — the rage and the horror — and what it means.
